userStories.title: Enforce opencode read-only ACP profiles through launch-time permission config
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Enable opencode ACP sessions for none, read and review by injecting an immutable per-profile permission policy at every process launch.

**Motivation** — So opencode can run only implementer-shaped sessions.

**Approach** — Integration targets (the Target is the interface to implement, not the existing baseline):

- `ReadOnlyEnforcement` (`packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/registry.ts`)
  - Target: `{ mode: ModeSetting | undefined; disallowedTools; sessionOptions; launchEnv: Readonly<Partial<Record<"none" | "read" | "review", Readonly<Record<string, string>>>>> }`. `launchEnv` holds variables added to the agent process's environment when the session's profile is that key. `freezeReadOnly` freezes `launchEnv` and each inner record, and copies `mode` only when defined. The Claude and codex entries declare `launchEnv: {}`.
- Registry entry `opencode`
  - Target: same launch and auth env; `readOnly: { mode: undefined, disallowedTools: [], sessionOptions: {}, launchEnv: { none: { OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT: OPENCODE_NONE_CONFIG }, read: { OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT: OPENCODE_READ_CONFIG }, review: { OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT: OPENCODE_REVIEW_CONFIG } } }`; `defaultMode` and `preApproval` undefined.
- New exported function `launchEnvFor(profile, entry)` in `capabilities.ts`, beside `modeFor`: returns `entry.readOnly.launchEnv[profile]` for `none`/`read`/`review` when present, otherwise `{}` (including `full`, `ask`, an entry without `readOnly`, and `entry` undefined).
- `openAcpSession` (`packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/open.ts`)
  - Target: launches with `env: { ...options.env, ...launchEnvFor(ctx.profile, options.entry) }`. The enforcement value wins over a caller-supplied variable of the same name, so a model's own `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` cannot weaken a read-only session. Every launch goes through `openAcpSession` (new session, resume, and the reconnect after the agent process dies), so every launch of the session carries it.

Symbols this feature only reads:

- `decidePermission(request, ctx)` in `packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/permissions.ts`: under `review`, an `execute` request is rejected with `REVIEW_NO_SANDBOX_REASON` when `ctx.sandbox` is undefined; a non-`execute` request is rejected with `readOnlyReason("review")`. Unchanged.
- `routerFor(ctx, secrets, entry)` in `backend.ts` and `sandboxFor(ctx, entry)` in `open.ts` give the permission layer a sandbox only when `entry?.preApproval` is defined. opencode has no `preApproval`, so under `review` every shell command opencode asks about is rejected with `REVIEW_NO_SANDBOX_REASON`. Unchanged.
- `modeFor(profile, entry)` in `capabilities.ts` returns `entry.readOnly.mode` for `none`/`read`/`review`; `applyMode` in `open.ts` skips the `session/set_config_option` call when that mode is undefined.
- `unmetRequirement(record, req)` refuses a read-only profile when `record.readOnlyMode` is false; `buildCapabilityRecord` sets `readOnlyMode` to `entry?.readOnly !== undefined`.

### Permission policy constants (`registry.ts`)

Exported strings, each the `JSON.stringify` of the object shown, keys in this order (opencode rules are last-match-wins, so `"*"` must come first):

```typescript
/** none: no tool at all. */
export const OPENCODE_NONE_CONFIG = JSON.stringify({ permission: { "*": "deny" } });
/** read: only opencode's read tools. */
export const OPENCODE_READ_CONFIG = JSON.stringify({
  permission: { "*": "deny", read: "allow", glob: "allow", grep: "allow", list: "allow" },
});
/** review: the read tools, plus shell commands asked of nax (decided by the review rule). */
export const OPENCODE_REVIEW_CONFIG = JSON.stringify({
  permission: { "*": "deny", read: "allow", glob: "allow", grep: "allow", list: "allow", bash: "ask" },
});
```

### Failure Handling

| Situation | Behaviour |
|:---|:---|
| A read-only opencode session's model tries a write or shell tool under `none`/`read` | The tool is not in opencode's catalog; the model reports it cannot, and the turn completes. Nothing reaches nax. This is opencode's own behaviour: no AC here; covered by the billed live check named in Out of Scope. |
| opencode asks to run a shell command under `review` | Rejected with `REVIEW_NO_SANDBOX_REASON`; opencode reports "The user declined this tool call" to the model and the turn continues. |
| The model def's env already sets `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` and the profile is `none`/`read`/`review` | The enforcement value replaces it. |
| The model def's env sets `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` and the profile is `full` or `ask` | The model's value is passed through unchanged. |

**Scope** — In: registry policy/data freezing, launchEnvFor, the launch env merge, registry/capability unit assertions and fake-agent integration tests. Put this story's integration tests in a new `test/unit/client/backend-opencode.test.ts`. Claude and codex behaviour does not change. In `test/unit/client/registry.test.ts`, move opencode out of the "%s: launch candidates and auth env; no read-only enforcement, no pre-approval" table into its own test; gemini and pi stay. Add `launchEnv: {}` to the exact Claude/codex expectations. Replace "every entry declaring read-only enforcement sets a mode (nax#2372)" with the mode-or-launchEnv invariant. Extend `test/unit/client/capabilities.test.ts` for the new selector and mode-less enforcement. The seam ACs enter at `createAgentSession` with `acpBackend({ agent: "opencode" })` and assert on the recorded launch request. Use `_acpBackendDeps.launch` and the in-memory fake; follow the resumable crash pattern for the reconnect assertion.

Out: US-002 owns nax config/schema defaults, OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR isolation, composed env helpers, manager/model-selection wiring and user documentation. Do not introduce plan mode, an opencode pre-approval channel, embedder tools support, or a sandbox for opencode; full/ask policies remain unchanged. Real-opencode catalog behavior and billed verification remain maintainer-only, not fake-agent claims.

**Scope** — Out (feature-level boundaries retained verbatim):
- Read-only enforcement for gemini and pi (the rest of nathapp-io/nax#2372); this spec does not close that issue.
- Selecting opencode's `plan` agent, or any opencode mode, for read-only profiles: the injected permission policy is the enforcement and nax sends no `session/set_config_option` for `mode` on opencode.
- Profiles `full` and `ask` on opencode: unchanged, opencode's own default permissions apply (its default agent writes and runs commands without asking), and nax injects no permission policy for them.
- Running shell commands for an opencode reviewer: opencode has no sandbox nax can deliver, so every shell command under `review` is rejected (accepted 2026-10-17); nax's embedder sandbox is never applied to opencode.
- Embedder tools (the loopback MCP tool host) on opencode: opencode has no pre-approval channel, so a session with tools is still refused with capability `tools`.
- Reads outside the session's working directory under `read`/`review`: opencode classifies them as its `external_directory` action, which the policy denies.
- A billed live check against a real opencode process: a maintainer step after merge.

**Interface** — Implement the registry interface with existing fields retained and the following mode/launchEnv contract:

```typescript
export interface ReadOnlyEnforcement {
  readonly mode: ModeSetting | undefined;
  readonly disallowedTools: readonly string[];
  readonly sessionOptions: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
  readonly launchEnv: Readonly<Partial<Record<"none" | "read" | "review", Readonly<Record<string, string>>>>>;
}
```

`launchEnvFor(profile, entry)` is exported beside `modeFor`, accepts an `AgentSessionProfile` and `AgentRegistryEntry | undefined`, and returns the selected readonly env record or `{}`. Do not change `modeFor`, `unmetRequirement`, `buildCapabilityRecord`, `decidePermission`, `routerFor` or `sandboxFor` behavior.

Reconnect test pattern (AC on the relaunch env): read `packages/nax-agent-acp/test/unit/client/backend-reconnect.test.ts` for its `RESUMABLE` fake script (advertises session resume so the backend reconnects) and the `fake.crash()` call between turns.

routing.reasoning: The production change is bounded to three existing modules with a pure env selector and launch merge, leaving permission and reconnect algorithms unchanged; security-critical session access control nevertheless requires strict three-session TDD, and the explicit existing-pattern integration fits the balanced native-deepseek profile.

modifiedFiles.reason: `ReadOnlyEnforcement.mode` becomes optional and `launchEnv` is added; `freezeReadOnly` freezes it; the Claude and codex entries declare `launchEnv: {}`; the three `OPENCODE_*_CONFIG` constants are exported and the opencode entry gets its `readOnly`.
adds `launchEnvFor`; `modeFor` is unchanged and returns `undefined` for an entry whose `readOnly.mode` is undefined.

the table test "%s: launch candidates and auth env; no read-only enforcement, no pre-approval" lists opencode with `readOnly: undefined`, so opencode moves out of that table into its own test asserting the new `readOnly` (gemini and pi stay); the Claude and codex exact-entry tests gain `launchEnv: {}` in their expected `readOnly`; and the test "every entry declaring read-only enforcement sets a mode (nax#2372)" fails for opencode, so it is replaced by a test that every entry declaring `readOnly` either sets a `readOnly.mode` with non-empty `configId` and `value` or declares a non-empty `launchEnv` record for each of `none`, `read` and `review`.

analysis:
This is an enhancement to two existing TypeScript packages, not a greenfield implementation. The binding decomposition is exactly US-001 in packages/nax-agent-acp and US-002 in packages/nax, each with dependencies []. They can be implemented independently: the first adds process-level permission enforcement, the second adds optional config-directory isolation. No package version changes, dependencies, persistence migrations, or public transport changes are required. Codebase-memory MCP tools were unavailable, so discovery used direct reads and targeted text searches. References below describe the pre-change checkout.

Architecture and constraints: docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:147 describes the package boundary: nax bundles nax-agent-acp and imports it only through @nathapp/nax-agent-acp/client; nax-agent-acp uses nax-agent's public entry. The ACP package must remain Node-compatible with no Bun APIs in src; nax uses its established _deps seams and package-scoped bun:test helpers. The architecture index and quick reference prescribe injectable external effects, centralized permissions, and no growth of oversized files (docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:20, docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:157). Never start a real ACP adapter in the unit suite. The live opencode evidence in the spec is a design premise, not something to reproduce with a billed process in automated tests.

US-001 current behavior and impact: ReadOnlyEnforcement currently requires a ModeSetting and has no launchEnv (packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/registry.ts:30). freezeReadOnly currently always spreads and freezes mode (registry.ts:56-67); spreading undefined would manufacture an empty object, so explicitly preserve undefined rather than freezing an empty mode. entry() freezes all registry policy data (registry.ts:70-84). Claude uses default mode plus removed write tools/settings; codex uses read-only mode without pre-approval; opencode currently has no policy and launches opencode acp with no auth variables (registry.ts:86-120). Add the three ordered JSON.stringify permission constants and profile-specific immutable launchEnv records; add empty launchEnv records to Claude/codex without changing their existing mode, sessionOptions, disallowedTools, launch candidates, auth variables, or default/pre-approval values. The new launchEnv map and every supplied inner env must be copied and frozen.

outOfScope: Read-only enforcement for gemini and pi (the rest of nathapp-io/nax#2372); this spec does not close that issue.
Selecting opencode's `plan` agent, or any opencode mode, for read-only profiles: the injected permission policy is the enforcement and nax sends no `session/set_config_option` for `mode` on opencode.
Profiles `full` and `ask` on opencode: unchanged, opencode's own default permissions apply (its default agent writes and runs commands without asking), and nax injects no permission policy for them.

Running shell commands for an opencode reviewer: opencode has no sandbox nax can deliver, so every shell command under `review` is rejected (accepted 2026-10-17); nax's embedder sandbox is never applied to opencode.
Embedder tools (the loopback MCP tool host) on opencode: opencode has no pre-approval channel, so a session with tools is still refused with capability `tools`.
Reads outside the session's working directory under `read`/`review`: opencode classifies them as its `external_directory` action, which the policy denies.

Copying or translating any part of the user's opencode config (providers, plugins, MCP servers, agents, the default model) into the isolated config dir; a provider defined only in the user's config is not available to an isolated session.
Removing or cleaning the isolated config dir; it is created once and reused.
An opencode version that renames its read tools or its `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` / `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` variables; nax does not detect it, and a renamed read tool is simply denied.
A `complete()` call that reaches opencode only as a fallback agent: the fallback resolver supplies its own model def, so that call gets no `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`.
Updating the package context file `.nax/mono/packages/nax-agent-acp/context.md` to say opencode is read-only capable: a manual step after merge, since `.nax/` is read-only to the run.
A billed live check against a real opencode process: a maintainer step after merge.
